The speaker suggests that Etsy's value proposition is currently challenging due to changing behaviors, but notes that the jury is still out and there is still time left for the company.

thesis: The episode argues that Meta is a strong buy because its core revenue drivers (users, time spent, impressions) are resilient and manageable, while the market is unfairly pricing in stagnation or decline. Conversely, Etsy faces significant headwinds from competitors like Temu that threaten its value proposition and advertising effectiveness, though the speaker leaves room for uncertainty on its future viability.

claims.claim: The speaker argues that Meta's revenue drivers (users, time spent, impressions, prices) were resilient, noting time spent increased with Reels and total users globally never went down.
claims.quote: And especially with Reels, it was increasing. And they were giving us that data point. So that's the first thing. You don't have to worry about time spent. The second thing, users, again, an easy one. They give us those numbers. Users were not leaving. At least, again, in aggregate. You can cut it up and say maybe US users under 30 were leaving Facebook, but total users globally were still increas

claims.claim: The speaker believes Meta was able to grow and that their AI capabilities allowed them to do a lot with less data, better than any competitor.
claims.quote: And their AI was able to do a lot with less data, better than, of course, any competitor. But that doesn't mean had ATT have not have happened, their ads wouldn't have been even better and more targeted. But nevertheless, it does seem now we can say that it wasn't all just maintenance CAPX. They clearly are able to grow now again.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests that looking at the facts of Meta, one shouldn't think it is in the 'too hard pile' and that a reverse DCF showed it didn't need a lot of faith to work out.
claims.quote: I mean, the good thing about that reverse DCF that you ran is you could see that you didn't need to have a lot of beliefs or a lot of faith for it to work out. I mean, obviously it worked out in a way that I don't think many people would have obviously predicted otherwise the stock price would have been reflected.

claims.claim: The speaker pushes back on the idea that Meta's situation was a 'hairball of a tornado' and argues that if you evaluate risks individually, you can see how they impact Meta.
claims.quote: And I think to some extent, that's what happened is people looked at all these risks. And rather than evaluating them individually and how they could actually impact meta, they kind of just looked at it as some sort of hairball of a tornado and just punted it.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Meta controls how many ads they show in the feed, and as long as people are entertained, they will continue to scroll, allowing Meta to show ads.
claims.quote: Who controls how much ads they show in the feed? It's essentially meta. As long as people are still entertained with whatever they're showing on the app, they're going to continue to scroll through and the meta is going to be able to show them an ad. We have ample history of that being the case.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests Etsy's core value proposition is under threat from competitors like Temu because consumers do not value Etsy's handmade and unique items enough to ignore cheaper alternatives, indicating a potential decline in growth.
claims.quote: And so that, to me, of course, is problematic because their value prop, their core value prop, they cannot change much. It's always going to be handmade. It's always going to be unique, idiosyn. And, you know, long shipping, that's a Piedin. They can't pull that out.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Etsy is facing headwinds from competitors like Temu, which is impacting their advertising effectiveness and suggesting that consumer preferences are shifting away from Etsy's offerings.
claims.quote: And so again, you talk about the pendulum, right, which is, hey, can they become more top of mind? Can they increase average buyer spend? And you're starting to see these little facts, right? You know, several years of investing in marketing, not seeing a lot of growth from that, you know, kind of calling out TEMU as a headwind to growth.

claims.claim: The speaker expresses concern that Etsy's TAM might be smaller than assumed, as consumers have a limit to how much they care about handmade goods, and the company is struggling with getting the right exploratory search and AI recommendations.
claims.quote: And I think there's some fears that that could be Etsy, where the thing they're really good at, people ultimately have a limit to how much they care about. Having said that, you're still only looking at $10 to $10 to $12 billion in, you know, quote unquote, handmade GMV globally.

claims.claim: The speaker defends the decision to buy META at $90 in December 2020, arguing that the stock was undervalued and that the company's ad tech capabilities allowed it to grow the digital ad market significantly despite privacy changes.
claims.quote: And, you know, we talk about Etsy and an average buyer growth growing. What was that kind of similar crux for meta? Yeah. And I think this is important because every investment is probabilistic, right? And so the question we're basically asking is just because we're, we're observing one outcome, what was actually the probability distribution?

claims.claim: The speaker highlights META's strength in direct response advertising, where advertisers can measure effectiveness in real-time, and notes that META's ability to match and measure ads grew the digital ad market from $30 billion to hundreds of billions.
claims.quote: With direct response ads, which is what meta specializes in, people would literally click the ad and almost in real time, they're able to measure whether or not these advertisements are effective or not. This was a totally new kind of advertising at the time. If you recall from our conversation, this exploded the digital ad market.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Apple's privacy changes and the ATT scare could negatively impact META's ad recommendation engine and ability to measure ad effectiveness, potentially reducing return on ad spend.
claims.quote: What happened with meta was, you see right at the same time as ATT is happening that Apple privacy changes are happening, which is it's confusing people exactly how much signal meta is ultimately going to be able to get from their users. Does this mess up their ad recommendation engine?

claims.quote: And so two of those risk factors, you've just eliminated users and time spent. And then, okay, so we have two more left. We have impressions and we have prices, ad prices. And another easy one, add impressions.

claims.quote: And so at that juncture would have had to believe that meta is not only not going to grow, they're actually going to shrink. And that wouldn't, I could see how someone could have thought that, especially given how much direct response ads have grown the digital ad market.
